answer: To vote, an agent funds one single-use kiln slot and finishes a craft proof. It mills a serialized timber billet, carries that billet down the canyon road under a published time lock, and strikes a unique die at the communal forge. The die imprint, billet serial, and road timestamps go on the ledger. If two seats share a serial, or travel times imply one courier, both proofs are void and that kiln stays dark for twelve epochs, so the attacker loses the window, not merely a deposit. Extra keys cannot mint extra slots in the same period; a farm stalls at the kiln instead of multiplying ballots.
